column1: # The counted classes of tools/audit-type-system.sh, and the number each one is allowed to have.
# **This is a dated measurement, not a ratchet — and this header claimed otherwise until it was
# corrected** (AUDIT F-16). Until 2026-09-27 the gate compared each class to the number here in *both*
# directions and failed the build on either. That comparison was removed with the rest of the gate
# apparatus, and nothing has read these numbers since: `ratchet_failures` in
# `tools/audit-type-system.sh` is declared and never incremented, and the script's own closing line
# says the counted classes "are reported above and not enforced".
# So read the numbers below as a measurement with a date — useful for asking "how much of this class
# was there, and is it going up?" — and *not* as a bound anything enforces. A class sitting at its
# baseline is not evidence that it cannot rise. Restoring the ratchet is a decision to take
# deliberately; until it is taken, this is the honest description of what the file is.
# Measured 2026-09-26 by the gate itself (`bash tools/audit-type-system.sh`), at `6b7a7f494`+C98;
# `cast` and `div` re-measured and reviewed the same day at `1078a824c` (see the paragraph below).
# Regenerate by running the gate after a change: it prints the measured value in the FAIL message.
# Two of these classes did not exist before that date. The audit pass of 2026-09-26 found the gate's
# scope to be panic/unsafe/silent/escape (hard) and cast/lax/get (soft, printed, never compared), so
# **variable indexing, slice ranges and division had no class at all** and overflow existed only as
# clippy's opinion — while `spec/TYPE-SYSTEM.md` §1.6's "no silent partiality" is the claim this gate
# is cited as enforcing. The counts are large because the classes are legal Rust; what is not legal is
# one *arriving unremarked*.
# `get` is 0 as of the split: its pattern used to carry `\b[a-zA-Z_]+\[[0-9]+\]` alongside the
# accessor form, and that alternative was all of it (measured: accessor half 0, index half 95 of 95).
# The index half is the `index` class now, counted properly at 313 rather than at the 95 that a
# literal-index-only pattern could see.
# **`cast` 332→336 and `div` 49→50, reviewed 2026-09-26 — the five sites are not this pass's.** They
# arrived with the merge of PR #67 (`016989af6`), *after* the measurement above, so the ratchet has
# been failing at step 1 of `test & coverage` on every commit since C98 — the register gate, the test
# suite and the coverage floor never ran behind it, which is how a green-looking audit series carried
# a red job. Each site, reviewed rather than waved through:
#   casper/src/merging.rs:515,541  `guard.len() as u64`            — `usize` → `u64` is *widening* on
#   casper/src/merging.rs:539      `pruned as u64`                   every target the node builds for,
#   casper/src/merging.rs:633      `elapsed().as_millis() as u64`    and the values are the
#                                                                    `Relaxed` observability counters
#                                                                    of the block-index cache (read
#                                                                    back at `:978`). The millis one is
#                                                                    a `u128` → `u64` narrowing, and
#                                                                    truncating it needs ~584 million
#                                                                    years of replay; it is a
#                                                                    diagnostic that never reaches
#                                                                    consensus.
#   node/src/runtime/node_runtime.rs:639  `stats.calls % 250`      — a log throttle: a counter modulo
#                                                                    a non-zero literal. The `div` class
#                                                                    flags it because a regex cannot
#                                                                    judge intent, which is the case
#                                                                    for a human reading it.
# Raise rather than fix, deliberately: the fix would be to rewrite another PR's freshly merged
# diagnostics from inside an audit unit, and would swap `as u64` for `try_from(..).unwrap_or(u64::MAX)`
# — a silent saturation in a metric, which is worse than the cast it replaces. The doctrine above is
# that these classes are legal Rust and what is *not* legal is a site **arriving unremarked**; this
# paragraph is the remark. `overflow` stays 41: the pass's own arithmetic (AUDIT C100's depth walk) is
# written `saturating_add`, so it adds no site — a ratchet is for sites someone reviewed, and that one
# needs no review.
# div 53 -> 54 (AUDIT C143's message, reviewed and raised 2026-09-27). The site is
# `node/src/configuration/configuration.rs:288`, and it is **not a division at all**: it is the
# substring `HTTP/2` inside the multi-line `format!` that refuses the nine settings this port parses
# and enforces nowhere. The pattern is `[a-zA-Z0-9_)]+[[:space:]]*[/%][[:space:]]*[a-zA-Z0-9_(]`, so
# `P/2` in a protocol name reads as one — the class the gate cannot judge, exactly as the
# `stats.calls % 250` throttle above does. **Raise rather than fix**: the honest fixes are to respell
# the protocol ("HTTP 2") in operator-facing text, which makes the message worse, or to teach the
# pattern that `HTTP/` is a name, which is a rule about prose and not about arithmetic. The stripper
# is why this arrives here rather than being filtered: it empties *single-line* string literals
# (`gsub(/"[^"]*"/, "")`, and its own comment records the approximation), so a `\`-continued literal
# spanning five lines keeps the lines that hold no closing quote. Measured: this commit's C142 change
# moves nothing, and the count was re-measured at `a3f850747^` (53, green) and `a3f850747` (54), which
# is where the site arrived — the rise was carried by a commit that touched no arithmetic and did not
# re-run the gate, the failure mode the paragraph above about PR #67 records twice already.
# div 50 -> 53 (AUDIT C113), raised deliberately. The three are the aggregate stream budget's own
# arithmetic in `comm/src/transport/grpc_transport_receiver.rs`: `content_data.len().div_ceil(unit)`
# and its two companions `stream_byte_budget(..) / STREAM_BUDGET_UNIT` in the test and production
# constructors. Each divisor is a non-zero `const`, so the class the gate cannot judge (a variable
# divisor that might be zero) does not arise at any of them; they are the metering arithmetic that
# makes the budget divide into `u32` permits, and they are new because the bound is new.
# `cast`/`index`/`overflow` are unmoved.
# `index` 313 -> 316 (AUDIT C124), raised deliberately, and the three sites are one construction.
# `subset_count` fills Pascal's row for `n` in place — `row[k]`, `row[k - 1]` and the `row[lo..=hi]`
# slice — because the alternative needs a division, which is the class above this one. The indices are
# bounded by the loop (`k` runs `1..=i` with `i <= n == row.len() - 1`), so the class the gate cannot
# judge (an index whose bound it cannot see) does not arise; this is a triangle computed in place and
# reviewed as such. **`cast` is unmoved by this pass**: it reads 331 below its recorded 336 because
# another session's in-flight work is in the tree, not because of C124 — the same churn the register
# rosters show, and the number returns to its baseline when that lands.
# `cast` 336 -> 331, lowered deliberately, and the five are not one change: **one is C124's** — the
# old `subset_count` narrowed three values to `u64` and the Pascal form narrows two to `usize` — and
# **four arrived with the other session's `block_api_impl.rs` work** (C129), which is in the tree and
# committed. The ratchet only goes down, so a fall is recorded the same way a rise is: the number is
# the tree's, and the paragraph says who put it there.
# class
cast
lax
get
index
div
overflow
